statement: Under current § 174 (as amended by P.L. 119-21), FOREIGN research or experimental expenditures are charged to capital account and amortized ratably over the 15-year period beginning with the midpoint of the taxable year in which paid or incurred; under § 174A (effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024), DOMESTIC research or experimental expenditures are currently deductible, with an election to amortize ratably over a period of not less than 60 months beginning with the month the taxpayer first realizes benefits. For taxable years beginning after 2021 and before 2025, the prior § 174 text (recorded in the section's amendment notes) required the same midpoint-convention capitalization of domestic specified research expenditures over 5 years — a half-year of amortization in year one (10% of a 5-year amount), full years after, and the remaining half-year in year six.
caveat: Law in flux: this card records what the cited statutory text and amendment notes said on the checked date and does not assert currentness. Transition treatment of unamortized pre-2025 domestic amounts, retroactive small-business elections, software-development scoping, and the § 280C interaction with the § 41 credit are agency-guidance and facts questions outside this card.
